## Exploratory data analysis

For this section graph and find statistics for each of your predictor variables vs the response. You do not need to look at the predictor variables individually

## Variable 1: `cell_phones_per_100_ppl`

### Graph and description

```{r cell_phones_per_100_ppl v. demo graph}
d |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Democracy), y = cell_phones_per_100_ppl)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "democracy", y = "cell phone per 100 people")
```

Democratic countries have higher cell phone per 100 capita than the non-democratic ones. And the mid-quantiles are separated pretty well.

### Stats and description

```{r cell_phones_per_100_ppl v. demo stat}
d %>%
  group_by(Democracy) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(cell_phones_per_100_ppl)),
    mean = mean(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(cell_phones_per_100_ppl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Non-democratic countries have higher std.dev. than the democratic ones, and all quantiles are higher in democratic countries.

## Variable 2: `residential_energy_use_pctg`

### Graph and description

```{r residential_energy_use_pctg v. demo graph}
d |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Democracy), y = residential_energy_use_pctg)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "democracy", y = "residential energy use percentage")
```

The mid quantiles are also well separated: democratic countries have much lower residential energy use percentage.

### Stats and description

```{r residential_energy_use_pctg v. demo stat}
d %>%
  group_by(Democracy) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(residential_energy_use_pctg)),
    mean = mean(residential_energy_use_pctg, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(residential_energy_use_pctg, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(residential_energy_use_pctg, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(residential_energy_use_pctg, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),

    Q3 = quantile(residential_energy_use_pctg, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),

```

The grouped distribution is similar to the first one: democratic countries have overall better performance in all quantile and less standard deviation, since there's some physical and economic cap for the variable.

## Variable 3: `landlocked`

### Graph and description

```{r landlocked v. demo graph}
d |>
  filter(!is.na(Democracy)) |>
  count(landlocked, Democracy) |>
  group_by(landlocked) |>
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()
```

Coastline countries have lower proportion of non-democracy (0.46 vs. 0.58), but doesn't provide enough sufficient evidence to separate the democracy groups.

### Stats and description

```{r landlocked v. demo stat}
tab <- table(d$landlocked, d$Democracy)
tab

chisq.test(tab)

fisher.test(tab)
```

Democratic regimes were less common among landlocked countries (41.7%) than coastal countries (53.3%). However, this association was not statistically significant (Fisher’s exact test: OR = 0.63, 95% CI \[0.23, 1.68\], p = .369).

## Variable 5: `maternal_mortality`

### Graph and description

```{r maternal_mortality v. demo graph}
d |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Democracy), y = maternal_mortality)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "democracy", y = "maternal mortality")
```

Democratic countries have very little maternal mortality, and the spread is really compressed to the bottom, while having several outliers, and non-democratic countries also have some high-performance cases, (democratic states overlapping with all high-performance non-democratic states.)

### Stats and description

```{r maternal_mortality v. demo stat}

  group_by(Democracy) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(maternal_mortality)),
    mean = mean(maternal_mortality, na.rm = TRUE),

    max = max(maternal_mortality, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"

```

The std. dev. is much smaller in democratic countries, and performance is better in all quantiles.

## Which variable for single variable models?

From your exploratory data analsys, which variable will you use for the single variable models? Why? \## kNN classification

I think the best predictor might be the hdi, since it offers the most separating effect on democracy groups. And the others are mostly overlapping in a relatively large proportion.

### Single variable model

Make a kNN model using your best predictor variable \#### Model tuning to find k

```{r}
d_hdi <- d |>
  filter(!is.na(Democracy), !is.na(human_development_ind)) |>
  mutate(Democracy = as.factor(Democracy))

hdi_recipe <- recipe(Democracy ~ human_development_ind, data = d_hdi) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

set.seed(2005)
folds <- vfold_cv(d_hdi, v = 5)

knn_spec2 <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors=tune(),  weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("classification")
knn_wf<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(hdi_recipe)|>
  add_model(knn_spec2)
knn_grid <- tibble(neighbors = seq(from=3, to=31, by=2)) 
class_met=metric_set(accuracy)
knn_cv <- tune_grid(
  knn_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = knn_grid, metrics=class_met
)
cv_metrics_knn<-collect_metrics(knn_cv)
cv_metrics_knn

autoplot(knn_cv, metric = "accuracy")
best_k <- select_best(knn_cv, metric = "accuracy")
best_k
```

21 is the best k.

#### Model for best k 

```{r}
knn_spec<-nearest_neighbor(neighbors=21,  weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("classification")

knn_wf<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(hdi_recipe)|>
  add_model(knn_spec)

hdi_knn_class <- 
  knn_wf |> 
  fit(data = d_hdi)

hdi_knn_class
```

Confirms that 21 is the best k.

#### Model evaluation-accuracy, cv for overfitting

```{r}
hdi_results <- augment(hdi_knn_class, new_data = d_hdi)

hdi_results|>
  conf_mat(truth = Democracy, estimate = .pred_class)

hdi_metric<-hdi_results|>
  accuracy(truth = Democracy, estimate = .pred_class)

hdi_metric

cv_k_21=cv_metrics_knn|>
  filter(neighbors==21)

cv_k_21
```

### All variable model

Make a kNN model using all your predictor variables \#### Model tuning to find k using cv.

```{r}
d_all <- d |>
  filter(!is.na(Democracy), !is.na(cell_phones_per_100_ppl),
         !is.na(residential_energy_use_pctg), !is.na(landlocked),
         !is.na(human_development_ind), !is.na(maternal_mortality)) |>
  mutate(Democracy = as.factor(Democracy))

all_recipe <- recipe(Democracy ~ cell_phones_per_100_ppl + residential_energy_use_pctg +
                       landlocked + human_development_ind + maternal_mortality, data = d_all) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())|>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

set.seed(2005)
folds_all <- vfold_cv(d_all, v = 5)

knn_spec2 <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors=tune(),  weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("classification")

knn_wf_all<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(all_recipe)|>
  add_model(knn_spec2)

knn_grid <- tibble(neighbors = seq(from=3, to=31, by=2)) 
class_met=metric_set(accuracy)

knn_cv_all <- tune_grid(
  knn_wf_all,
  resamples = folds_all,
  grid = knn_grid, metrics=class_met
)

cv_metrics_knn_all<-collect_metrics(knn_cv_all)
cv_metrics_knn_all

autoplot(knn_cv_all, metric = "accuracy")
best_k_all <- select_best(knn_cv_all, metric = "accuracy")
best_k_all
```

Best k = 5

#### Model for best k

```{r}
knn_spec_all<-nearest_neighbor(neighbors=5,  weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("classification")

knn_wf_all<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(all_recipe)|>
  add_model(knn_spec_all)

all_knn_class <- 
  knn_wf_all |> 
  fit(data = d_all)

all_knn_class
```

#### Model evaluation-accuracy, cv for overfitting

```{r}
all_results <- augment(all_knn_class, new_data = d_all)

all_results|>
  conf_mat(truth = Democracy, estimate = .pred_class)

all_metric<-all_results|>
  accuracy(truth = Democracy, estimate = .pred_class)

all_metric

cv_k_all=cv_metrics_knn_all|>
  filter(neighbors==5)

cv_k_all
```

## Logistic Regression

### Single variable model

Make a logistic regression model using your best predictor variable \#### Model

```{r}
d_hdi|>
  pull(Democracy)|>
  levels()

log_rec<-
  recipe(Democracy~human_development_ind, data=d_hdi)

logit_mod <-
  logistic_reg()|>
  set_engine("glm")|>
  set_mode("classification")

glm_workflow <-
  workflow() |>
  add_recipe(log_rec)|>
  add_model(logit_mod)

hdi_fit <-
  glm_workflow |>
  fit(data = d_hdi)

tidy(hdi_fit)
```

#### Equation and Graph of model

```{r}
d_hdi <- d_hdi |>
  mutate(bin_demo=if_else(Democracy=="Yes",1,0))

ggplot(d_hdi, aes(x = human_development_ind, y = bin_demo)) + 
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.05), 
    alpha = 0.5
  ) + 
  geom_smooth(
    method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), 
    color = "dodgerblue", lty = 2, se = FALSE
  ) + 
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0.5), linetype = 3)
```
